paper_metadata.title: An introduction to financial option pricing on a qudit-based quantum computer

summary: This paper presents a qudit-based simulation of European call option pricing using probability loading, comparator logic, payoff encoding, and maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation without phase estimation. The reported simulation uses an 8-dimensional and a 10-dimensional asset register, N = 100 shots per m_l, T = 7, and M = 26200 oracle queries, and compares the quantum-simulated payoff against a classical finite-resource discretization and the analytic Black-Scholes-Merton payoff. The result is a theoretical quadratic scaling improvement over classical Monte Carlo, but only in noiseless simulation and for a path-independent option.

experiments.description: Numerical simulation of a qudit-based European call option pricing algorithm using probability loading, comparator, payoff encoding, and maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation without phase estimation.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation for qudit-based option pricing
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Estimate theta_P1 from likelihood maximization over measurement data collected for m_l = 0, 1, 3, 7, ... up to cutoff T

hyperparameters.strike_price_K: varies by simulation (1.7 in Fig. 6, 2.2 in Fig. 7)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not applicable; no variational parameters. Measurement data used in MLE.
classical_baselines: Classical Monte Carlo integration discussed as baseline

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Asset price ST discretized into dn basis states of an n-qudit register; each basis state |i> encodes a sampled asset price s_i via affine map s_i = S_min + (i + 1/2) omega. Payoff loaded into a separate ancilla qubit via controlled Y rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Price a European call option with payoff f(ST)=max(0, ST-K) and fair value nu = e^{-rT} E_P[f(ST)]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator qubit separates i<k and i>=k cases; payoff is approximated by shifted/scaled Y rotations; no explicit penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: European call option under Black-Scholes-Merton log-normal asset-price model

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic log-normal distribution with parameters S0, alpha, sigma, T; discretized over [S_min, S_max]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate asset-price domain to [S_min, S_max] using approximately mean ± 3 standard deviations; discretize into dn equal intervals; sample at interval midpoints; normalize sampled probabilities
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulation over varying qudit Hilbert-space dimensions; compare quantum-simulated payoff against classical finite-resource discretization and analytic payoff; N=100 shots per m_l, T=7 in reported figures

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct discretized probability distribution from BSM model; compute Householder state-preparation matrix; build comparator and payoff-loading subroutines; generate measurement data for multiple Grover-operator powers
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use measurement counts to form binomial likelihoods and maximize likelihood for theta_P1; map estimated theta_P1 to P1 and then to expected payoff via Eq. 15

results.unit: m_0 = 0; subsequent values m_l = 2^l - 1 for l=1..T

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation without phase estimation; asymptotic regime
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that the advantage is theoretical and that path-independent European options are unlikely to benefit much in practice; NISQ hardware noise and circuit depth are additional caveats.

speedup_claims.conditions: using maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation without phase estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: M is the number of oracle calls; the paper states this scaling but does not provide a fitted empirical convergence curve.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(M^-1) estimation error for amplitude estimation without phase estimation
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: M = sum_{l=0}^T N(2m_l+1), reported as 26200 in simulations

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; the paper reports only simulated results for d=8 and d=10 and does not identify a crossover problem size.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation with M = 26200 oracle queries, N = 100 shots per m_l, and T = 7; the paper also notes the need for deep state-preparation and comparator circuits.
limiting_factors: No hardware experiment; only numerical simulation
State preparation and comparator subroutines are deep and resource-intensive
Paper notes phase estimation is a bottleneck and uses MLE instead
NISQ noise and compilation overhead are highlighted as practical barriers
European call option is path-independent and explicitly noted as unlikely to benefit much in practice

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the entire stack is numerically simulated with a custom Python package and does not name a real QPU.

num_qubits not explicitly given as a single total register size for the full circuit; the paper describes an n-qudit asset register plus comparator and payoff ancillas, but no concrete total qubit count is reported.
circuit_depth not reported as a single numeric value; only asymptotic comments and subroutine depth scaling are discussed.
The paper claims a theoretical quadratic speedup for amplitude estimation without phase estimation, but only demonstrates this in simulation.
Classical finite-resource discretization and analytic Black-Scholes-Merton values are used as baselines; no real quantum hardware advantage is shown.
